title: The envelope is written through a fixed .partial name and a bare rename
instrument: a vitest over an exported writeAtomically (or analyseTrack's write half) with node:fs/promises rename mocked to throw EPERM once, then succeed: A fails the analyse step, B lands the envelope; plus two concurrent writers to one target leaving one whole file
body:
## Summary
lib/sound/mv/render.ts writeAtomically stages to `${target}.partial` and renames with fs.rename, while the same context's lib/sound/mv/store.ts landFile stages to a pid+counter name and renames through lib/renameRetry.ts (JITTERED_RENAME) because Windows refuses a rename onto a file a reader holds.

## Description
Two implementations of 'land a file whole' in one context (lib/sound/mv/render.ts:97-102 vs lib/sound/mv/store.ts:134-157). The envelope (mv/<id>/envelope.json) is read back by every render and by the motion regenerate; on this Windows box a reader holding it (an indexer, a second render) turns the analyse step's rename into EPERM and fails the job, where every other file the queue lands retries. A fixed `.partial` name also means two writers of one envelope share a staging file. Fixed: writeAtomically stages through store.ts stagingAbs and lands through landFile.

## Flow
- analyse step -> analyseTrack -> writeAtomically(envelopePath) -> fs.rename while a reader holds envelope.json -> EPERM -> job failed at analyse
- fix: stagingAbs(rel) + landFile(staged, rel) (both already exported by ./store.ts)

## Expected impact
The operator sees fewer analyse-step failures on Windows; nothing else changes. Could break: nothing reads the `.partial` name.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the envelope lands like every other mv file
Before: 1 of 2 landing paths in the context retries a Windows EPERM (simulation: walked; analyseTrack needs a headless browser this round did not drive)
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - analyseTrack asserts a headless browser before writing, so no gate reached the write without a seam; the instrument above is that seam
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/sound/mv/render.ts:97-102 writeAtomically: const tmp = `${target}.partial`; await writeFile(tmp, bytes); await rename(tmp, target);
lib/sound/mv/store.ts:148-157 landFile: renameRetry(stagedAbs, abs, JITTERED_RENAME)

title: A staged file is left in the job folder when its own write fails
instrument: a vitest that mocks node:fs/promises writeFile/copyFile to create the staged file, write half, and throw ENOSPC, then drives runStep('still') and fetchAudio (take and clip) on a temp store and counts `*.partial.*` files left under mv/<id>/: A 3, B 0
body:
## Summary
Three of the five staging sites in lib/sound/mv clean up only when the LANDING fails, not when their own write does: steps.ts still (writeFile), fetchAudio.ts take (copyFile) and clip (writeFile).

## Description
lib/sound/mv/steps.ts:136-147 writes the staged still, then wraps only landing() in a try that removes it; lib/sound/mv/fetchAudio.ts:65-67 and :74-76 call copyFile/writeFile then landFile, whose catch removes the staged file only on a rename failure. The video step (steps.ts:155-163) wraps the engine call too, so it is the model the other three should follow. A disk-full write therefore leaves a `<name>.<pid>.<n>.partial.<ext>` beside the job's files, nobody points at it, and a retry writes a second one.

## Flow
- still step -> writeFile(staged) throws ENOSPC mid-write -> staged half-file stays in mv/<id>/ -> retry stages under a new counter name
- fix: one try around write+land in each site that rm's the staged path on any throw

## Expected impact
Litter in the store folder after a disk-full failure stops accumulating. Could break: nothing; the staged names are never read.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed step leaves no orphan file
Before: 3 of 5 staging sites leave the staged file on their own write failure (read)
After: 0 of 5 (predicted)
Method: simulation - a mid-write failure needs an fs seam this round did not build; the instrument is named
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: A dropped video's track reads 'skip-done' to the album batch
body:
## Summary
planBatch marks a track whose newest job is done as skip-done - 'its video exists' per batch.ts's header - including a job whose verdict is drop, whose video file Drop deleted.

## Description
lib/sound/mv/batch.ts:177-182 reads only newest.state; lib/sound/mv/queue.ts patchMv deletes the video of a dropped job (DROPPED_FILES) and keeps state done. So an album re-run after the operator dropped a track's video makes no new one unless --again, and --again re-makes every done track too. Whether a dropped track should be re-queued by a plain re-run (a new still: credits) is the operator's call, not a sweep's: it changes what a run spends.

## Flow
- drop a track's video on the Board -> rerun /music-video <folder> -> its row says skip-done -> no new video
- options: (a) a dropped newest job reads 'queue'; (b) a new 'skip-dropped' action the plan prints; (c) keep, and correct the header's 'its video exists'

## Expected impact
The operator re-running an album gets the dropped tracks redone, or told they were skipped as dropped. Could break: an unattended re-run starts spending on tracks the operator meant to abandon.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a re-run treats a dropped video as not made
Before: a dropped track reads skip-done (walked: batch.ts:177-182, queue.ts:291-299)
After: depends on the chosen option
Method: simulation - the decision is a spend direction; no instrument decides it
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: lib/sound/mv/batch.ts:23 'done skipped - its video exists'; :180 else if (newest?.state === "done" && !opts.again) action = "skip-done"; lib/sound/mv/store.ts:126 DROPPED_FILES includes video

title: A motion or metadata regenerate of a dropped video buys a new still
body:
## Summary
regenerateMv accepts a done record whatever its verdict; for a dropped one the still, audio and video files are gone, so packages/producers/src/mv/plan.ts planOf adds fetch, still and video to a 'metadata' or 'motion' redo - a new Leonardo still from the old prompt and a full render.

## Description
REDO_STEPS promises 'everything it does not name stays byte-identical' (packages/producers/src/mv/plan.ts:41); missingSteps (plan.ts:61-70) then re-adds every step whose output Drop deleted. The receipt prices it honestly (lib/producers/mv.ts mvLine: buysStill -> studio-still line), so nothing is spent unseen, but a 'metadata only' ask becomes a still purchase and a render. Whether a dropped video may be regenerated at all, or only by image, is a product call; the plan lives outside this context.

## Flow
- drop a video -> Regenerate · metadata -> receipt lists 'Leonardo studio still · 1080p render' -> confirm -> a new still is bought
- options: refuse motion/metadata regenerate of a dropped record (409), or keep and say so on the receipt line

## Expected impact
A metadata-only regenerate stays a text turn. Could break: an operator who regenerates a dropped track deliberately to get it back.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a part regenerate does only its part
Before: metadata redo on a dropped record plans fetch, still, metadata, video (walked planOf)
After: depends on the chosen rule
Method: simulation - a spend and product direction; plan.ts is out of this context
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: packages/producers/src/mv/plan.ts:41 REDO_STEPS doc; :61-70 missingSteps; lib/sound/mv/queue.ts:218 only done|failed checked; lib/sound/mv/store.ts:126 DROPPED_FILES
